entities.summary:
André Chénier was a French poet and playwright whose sensual, emotive poetry marked him as one of the precursors of the Romantic movement. Born in Istanbul on October 30, 1762, he returned to France at the age of 18 and quickly became associated with the events of the French Revolution. During this time, Chénier was a member of the Jacobin Club and served on the Paris Commune.

Chénier's poetry and writings were known for their passion, lyricism, and political fervor, but he was also accused of being a counter-revolutionary and was sentenced to death by guillotine in 1794. His execution marked the end of his career as a poet and playwright, leaving behind only his works, which have been celebrated for their beauty and emotional power.

Despite his tragic fate, Chénier's legacy has endured, inspiring generations of writers, artists, and intellectuals. His life and work continue to be studied by scholars and admired by readers around the world, offering a poignant reminder of the enduring power of art and imagination in times of turmoil and transformation.
